neighbours.label: determiner/preposition slot right after an event is said to take place, where a day or time of day is expected next ('held the first [weekend]', 'concert this [evening]', 'took place last [Sunday]')
fire: Every year the harvest festival is held on the third Saturday of September.
Our school band will be playing a short concert this afternoon in the gym.
The annual book sale takes place the first weekend of March at the library.
The city council met last night to vote on the new budget.
A charity run through the old town is planned for next Sunday.
The opening ceremony gets underway this morning on the main square.
In Sweden the midsummer feast is celebrated on the Friday nearest the solstice.
The orchestra performed two new pieces at the cathedral last weekend.
quiet: The harvest festival committee printed the third edition of its small cookbook.
Our school band has learned this piece by heart and plays it well.
The annual book sale filled the first floor of the library with boxes.
The city council read the last page of the new budget aloud.
A charity run needs volunteers at the next corner of the old town.
The opening ceremony used this stage and a borrowed sound system.
In Sweden the midsummer feast depends on the weather and the herring.
The orchestra placed the two new pieces in the second half of the program.

notes: Card: peaks on ' this', ' last', ' first', ' on', ' the' before weekend/Sunday/morning/night; output promotes ' weekend', ' Saturday', ' Sunday'. Probes: 0.5-0.87 for scheduled events, ~0.01 for the same determiners before non-time nouns. The - pole (' early', ' late' before morning/night) looks like the modifier side of the same time-of-day slot.
